'''Michel Armand''' (born 1946)<ref>{{cite web|title=History of Science and Recent Technology|url=https://authors.library.caltech.edu/5456/1/hrst.mit.edu/hrs/materials/public/Armand_biography.htm|publisher=The Dibner Institute for the History of Science and Technology}}</ref> is a French scientist who is best known for introducing the concept of
a [[rocking-chair battery]] in 1978.<ref>1978 NATO conference on Materials for Advanced Batteries, Aussios, France. Cited from ISBN 978-1-61249-762-4. page 94.</ref> In a rocking-chair battery, the same type of ion is de/intercalated into both positive and negative electrodes during dis/charge. As a result, solution-phase species do not appear in the reaction [[stoichiometry]], which allows for minimizing the amount of solvent in the battery, reduces the battery weight and cost.
<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Towards Efficient Energy Storage Materials: Lithium Intercalation/Organic Electrodes to Polymer Electrolytes-A Road Map (Tribute to Michel Armand)|journal=Journal of the Electrochemical Society|date=5 January 2020 |volume=167|issue=7 |pages=070530|doi=10.1149/1945-7111/ab787a|s2cid=216387031|last1=Shanmukaraj |first1=Devaraj |last2=Ranque |first2=Pierre |last3=Ben Youcef |first3=Hicham |last4=Rojo |first4=Teofilo |last5=Poizot |first5=Philippe |last6=Grugeon |first6=Sylvie |last7=Laruelle |first7=Stephane |last8=Guyomard |first8=Dominique |doi-access=free }}</ref>

Michel grew up in [[Annecy]], in the [[French Alps]], in a family of science teachers. In 1968, he graduated from [[Ecole Normale Supérieure]], where he became interested in [[electrochemistry]] and [[Electric battery|batteries]]. In 1970, he started his PhD studies at [[Stanford University]] with [[Robert Huggins]] as a [[Fulbright Scholar]]. [[Stanley Whittingham]] was a postdoc in the same laboratory at Stanford. Armand felt that the Stanford laboratory was overly focused on fundamental research, while he wanted to develop practical batteries. For this reason, he dropped out of Stanford's PhD program 18 months later and returned to France to finish his PhD at [[Université Joseph-Fourier]] in [[Grenoble]].<ref>Long Hard Road: The Lithium-Ion Battery and the Electric Car. 2022. C.J. Murray. ISBN 978-1-61249-762-4. p.96.</ref>

While in graduate school, Armand was determined to find a practical way to [[Intercalation (chemistry)|intercalate]] lithium and potassium ions into graphite. He found that solvent co-intercalation presented a problem with lithium ions. For this reason, he decided to try a solid polymer electrolyte and obtained a patent on this idea. However, the lack of a suitable positive intercalation electrode material prevented the commercialization of that invention at that time.<ref>Long Hard Road: The Lithium-Ion Battery and the Electric Car. 2022. C.J. Murray. ISBN 978-1-61249-762-4. p.97.</ref>

Lithium batteries are electrochemical devices that are widely used as power sources. The history of their development has contributions from many scientists. In particular, without the developments by Professor Michel Armand related to electrodes and electrolytes, the lithium batteries of today would not exist as the foundation for electronic devices.<ref name="Andrea Paolella">{{cite journal|title=Brief History of Early Lithium-Battery Development|year=2020|publisher=MDPI|pmc=7215417|last1=Reddy|first1=M. V.|last2=Mauger|first2=A.|last3=Julien|first3=C. M.|last4=Paolella|first4=A.|last5=Zaghib|first5=K.|journal=Materials|volume=13|issue=8|page=1884|doi=10.3390/ma13081884|pmid=32316390|bibcode=2020Mate...13.1884R|doi-access=free}}</ref>

He runs a research team in Spain at [[CIC energiGUNE]] and has had his work published in ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]''.<ref name="Issues and challenges facing rechargeable lithium batteries">{{cite journal|title=Issues and challenges facing rechargeable lithium batteries|year=2001|doi=10.1038/35104644|url=https://www.nature.com/articles/35104644|last1=Tarascon|first1=J.-M.|last2=Armand|first2=M.|journal=Nature|volume=414|issue=6861|pages=359–367|pmid=11713543|bibcode=2001Natur.414..359T |s2cid=2468398|url-access=subscription}}</ref>
